For any three positive real numbers a, b, and c, show that $a^2/b^2 + b^2/c^2 + c^2/a^2 \geq b/a + c/b + a/c$.
Continue from:
["Let \(x=a/b\), \(y=b/c\), \(z=c/a\). Then \(xyz=1\) and the desired inequality is equivalent to \(x^2+y^2+z^2\ge 1/x+1/y+1/z\).","With the same substitution one has \(1/x+1/y+1/z=xy+yz+zx\), so it suffices to prove \(x^2+y^2+z^2\ge xy+yz+zx\)."]
["The inequality \(x^2+y^2+z^2\ge xy+yz+zx\) is equivalent to \(\frac12\bigl((x-y)^2+(y-z)^2+(z-x)^2\bigr)\ge0\), which holds for all real \(x,y,z\).","Adding the three AM-GM inequalities \(x^2+y^2\ge2xy\), \(y^2+z^2\ge2yz\) and \(z^2+x^2\ge2zx\) immediately yields \(x^2+y^2+z^2\ge xy+yz+zx\)."]
["Since \(xyz=1\), we recover \(xy+yz+zx=1/x+1/y+1/z\), and therefore \(x^2+y^2+z^2\ge1/x+1/y+1/z\), which is the substituted form of the original inequality.","Equality holds if and only if \(x=y=z\), hence \(x=y=z=1\) (using \(xyz=1\)), which is equivalent to \(a=b=c\)."]
nodes.last_claim: ["Since \(xyz=1\), we recover \(xy+yz+zx=1/x+1/y+1/z\), and therefore \(x^2+y^2+z^2\ge1/x+1/y+1/z\), which is the substituted form of the original inequality.","Equality holds if and only if \(x=y=z\), hence \(x=y=z=1\) (using \(xyz=1\)), which is equivalent to \(a=b=c\)."]
